rulings.Rulings: Matter on the LAW AND MOTION / DISCOVERY CALENDAR FOR THURSDAY, JUL-06-2026. LINE 2. PLAINTIFF WELLS FARGO BANK, NA's Motion To Vacate Dismissal Under C.C.P. Section 664.6 & Enter Judgment Pursuant To Stipulation. Plaintiff Wells Fargo Bank. N.A.'s motion to vacate dismissal and enter judgment pursuant to stipulation. Wells Fargo has shown that it is entitled to have the dismissal vacated and to have judgment entered in its favor and against Lindsey Lonne in the amount of $30,080.88. No opposition filed to this motion. The court will sign the previously submitted proposed order and proposed judgment. For the 9:00 a.m. calendar, all attorneys and parties may appear in Department 301 remotely or in person. Remote hearings will be conducted by videoconference using Zoom. (Dept. 301 Zoom ID 161 502 4290; Passcode 700956.) To appear remotely at the hearing, go to the court's website at sfsuperiorcourt.org under "Online Services," navigate to "Tentative Rulings," and click on the appropriate link, or dial the corresponding phone number. Any party who contests a tentative ruling must send an email to contestdept301tr@sftc.org with a copy to all other parties by 4pm stating, without argument, the portion(s) of the tentative ruling that the party contests. The subject line of the email shall include the line number, case name and case number. The text of the email shall include the name and contact information, including email address, of the attorney or party who will appear at the hearing. The court no longer provides a court reporter in the Law & Motion or Discovery Department. Parties may retain their own reporter, who may appear in the courtroom or remotely. A retained reporter must be a California certified court reporter (CSR), for only a CSR's transcript may be used in California courts. If a CSR is being retained, include in your email all of the following: their name, CSR and telephone numbers, and their individual work email address. =(301/HEK)

rulings.Rulings: Matter on the LAW AND MOTION / DISCOVERY CALENDAR FOR THURSDAY, JUL-06-2026. LINE 3. PLAINTIFF CARTER FEDERAL CREDIT UNION's Motion For Order Deeming Request For Admissions To Defendant Admitted And For Monetary Sanctions. Plaintiff Carter Federal Credit Union's motion for order deeming that defendant Liane Dutton has admitted the set one requests for admission and for monetary sanctions is granted. Dutton is deemed to admit the set one requests for admissions. No later than September 30, 2026 Dutton must pay Carter FCU reasonable monetary sanctions of $310. Dutton's failure to respond to the requests for admission and her failure to file any opposition to this motion is sufficient to grant the motion and show lack of substantial justification for the sanctions award. rulings.Rulings: Matter on the LAW AND MOTION / DISCOVERY CALENDAR FOR THURSDAY, JUL-06-2026. LINE 4. 1-DEFENDANT SAN FRANCISCO UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT's, A PUBLIC ENTITY, DEMURRER to COMPLAINT. Defendant San Francisco Unified School District's demurrer to the fourth, tenth, and eleventh causes of action for disability discrimination, failure to accommodate, and failure to engage in an interactive process in the complaint filed by Conrad Tanasychuk is sustained with leave to amend by August 24, 2026 as to all three causes of actions. All three claims insufficiently allege ultimate facts showing that Tanasychuk's "work-related stress" is a "disability" per FEHA. Defendant San Francisco Unified School District's motion to strike the portions of the complaint filed by Conrad Tanasychuk alleging failure to prevent discrimination and violation of Labor Code 6310 is granted with leave to amend by August 24, 2026 as to all portions of the complaint sought to be stricken.
